sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 7.7% a year from $15.4 billion in FY2018 to $25.8 billion in FY2025 [F1][F8][F145], and operating income grew 9.9% a year [F146].
Net income grew only 0.4% a year, from $6.64 billion to $6.84 billion [F25][F32][F147].

Operating margin fell 14.6pp to 15.5% in FY2021 and rose 23.5pp to 41.3% in FY2023 [D107][F20][D177][F22]; the passages cited do not explain the operating-margin swings, though FY2023 NEER net income of $3.56 billion included about $1,729 million of non-qualifying hedge gains [S27][P30].
FY2024 revenue fell 5.2% [D201] as FPL storm cost recovery revenue dropped about $1,090 million and fuel cost recovery revenue about $526 million [P34].
FPL revenue was $18.2 billion in FY2025, 70.5% of the total, up 7.7% and contributing 5.5pp of the 9.8% revenue growth [S6][D271][D272][D273][D236].
FPL operating revenues rose $1,243 million, mainly on higher storm cost recovery, retail base and storm protection plan revenues, with storm cost recovery alone about $1,091 million [P21][P18].

FPL's share of revenue slipped from 76.5% in FY2020 to 70.5% in FY2025 [D258][D271]; the pack has no NEER revenue split, only NEER net income of $2.98 billion against $2.30 billion a year earlier [S29][S28].
NEER's result improved mainly on earnings from new wind, solar and battery projects, partly offset by higher financing costs [P26].
Operating leverage was thin in FY2025: operating expenses grew 10.0% against revenue growth of 9.8%, and the incremental operating margin was 34.8% [D249][D236][D256].
Diluted shares rose 0.6% while net income fell 1.6% and diluted EPS fell 2.1% [D251][D238][D240].

FY2018 and FY2019 per-share data are on a pre-split basis (diluted shares 477.0 million versus 1,968.8 million in FY2020) after a 2020 stock split, so I draw no conclusion from the EPS CAGR [X67][X69][P74].
Operating margin of 32.1% in FY2025 sits above the window median of 30.3% and well below the 41.3% high, with a low of 15.5% [F24][D300][D299][D298].
It rose 0.3pp in FY2025 while D&A climbed to 25.5% of revenue from 23.2% [D247][D224][D189].
FPL depreciation and amortization rose $951 million, primarily on about $1,090 million of higher amortization of deferred storm costs from Hurricanes Debby, Helene and Milton [P16].
Net margin of 26.5% is below operating margin because other expense was $3.75 billion [F40][F24][X64].
Corporate and Other results fell $1,256 million, primarily on about $1,002 million of unfavorable after-tax non-qualifying hedge activity on interest rate derivatives plus higher average debt [P8].
The effective tax rate moved to -17.7% from 5.6% [D226][D191], and FPL income taxes fell $251 million on higher clean energy tax credits [P15].
Operating cash flow of $12.5 billion was 1.83x net income, below 1.91x in FY2024 and 2.16x in FY2019 [F64][D227][D192][D17].
It fell 5.8% and dropped to 48.4% of revenue from 56.4% [D241][D225][D190].
Investing outflow of $23.9 billion was 1.9 times operating cash flow, and the pack has no separate capex line, so free cash flow is not computed [F72][F64].
The shift from net over-recovery to under-recovery of cost recovery clauses cut FPL operating cash flow by about $89 million, mainly on higher fuel prices [P19].
Net debt reached $92.2 billion in FY2025 from $80.6 billion, on total debt of $95.0 billion and cash of $2.81 billion [D231][D196][D230][D229].
Net cash was -357.4% of revenue, the 0th percentile among four utilities peers, whose median is -228.4% [D232][D314][D315].
The current ratio of 0.60x is the window high, helped by current debt falling to $3.50 billion from $8.06 billion [F128][D305][X106][X105].
Debt issued was $23.4 billion against $10.3 billion repaid, and dividends of $4.68 billion were 68.5% of net income; the pack shows no buyback line [X90][X98][D233][F32].
Return on average equity of 13.1% is the 100th percentile of four peers, whose median is 11.6% [D235][D316][D317].
Those returns rest on a balance sheet where long-term debt grew 23.7% against equity growth of 9.0% [D245][D244].
[R2] Net debt has widened seven years in a row, from $34.3 billion in FY2018 to $92.2 billion in FY2025 [D9][D231].
Higher average debt is already named as a drag on Corporate and Other results [P8].
[R1] The current ratio was below 1.0x in every year of the window, at 0.60x in FY2025 [F121][F128].
Liquidity therefore depends on continued access to debt markets, which makes the net debt build more important.
[R4] Pretax income fell to $4.53 billion from $6.04 billion while net income fell only 1.6%, cushioned by a $802 million tax benefit [X48][X47][D238][X56].
Net income is leaning on clean energy tax credits, which rose about $585 million at NEER [P11].
Data quality: the 2020 stock split leaves FY2018 and FY2019 per-share figures on a different basis from later years, so the long-run EPS CAGR is unreliable [X67][X69][P74][F149].
Operating margin falling below the window median of 30.3%, from 32.1% now, would reverse the stable-margin reading (FY2026 10-K) [D300][F24].
Net cash as a share of revenue worsening beyond -357.4%, with net debt above $92.2 billion, would confirm continued leverage build (FY2026 10-K) [D232][D231].
With the FY2025 effective tax rate at -17.7% [D226], a move back toward the 5.6% rate of FY2024 [D191] would pressure the FY2025 net margin of 26.5% (FY2026 10-K) [F40].
A current ratio falling below the window median of 0.52x from 0.60x would reverse the liquidity improvement (FY2026 10-K) [D306][F128].
